questions.question: Explain the significance of conservation of angular momentum in the case of Earth-Moon system.
questions.solution_html:
• Moon system.
  • The Moon’s gravity raises two tidal bulges on Earth, and because Earth Conservation
  • rotates faster than the Moon orbits, the bulge nearest the Moon is dragged of angular
  • slightly ahead. This creates a gravitational torque that slows down Earth’s momentum
  • rotation, decreasing its rotational angular momentum. At the same time, this only (1 mark)
  • torque transfers angular momentum to the Moon, causing it to move
  • gradually farther away from Earth and increase its orbital angular
  • momentum. Although Earth’s rotation slows, the total angular momentum of
  • the Earth–Moon system remains constant, and over billions of years, this
  • process will continue until Earth’s day becomes equal to the Moon’s orbital
  • period, making one day as long as one month.
questions.final_answer: period, making one day as long as one month
